approved: Moved the second reading of the companion Homelessness (Consequential Amendments) Bill, which repeals the Supported Accommodation Assistance Act 1994 and updates the definition of homeless person in the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 so that people experiencing homelessness can continue to enrol and vote using provisions introduced in 2010.

Argued that the Homelessness Bill 2013 is aspirational and adds no funding, citing a 17 per cent rise in homelessness from 89,728 in 2006 to 105,237 in 2011 despite Labor's pledge to halve it by 2020, criticised a $159 million one-year funding deal as a bandaid, and said a coalition government would provide a $1.5 billion mental health package.

Argued that the Homelessness Bill 2013 offers only aspiration without funding, citing a 17 per cent rise in homelessness from 89,728 in 2006 to 105,237 in 2011 despite Labor's pledge to halve it by 2020, and noted the government's $159 million one-year funding deal and pledged a coalition government would provide a $1.5 billion mental health package instead.

Argued that the Homelessness Bill 2013, drawing on the white paper The Road Home and a 2009 parliamentary inquiry, complements existing funding to advance the government's target of halving homelessness by 2020, and announced work with the states on a non-legislative Homelessness National Quality Framework.
